objective: Give the mesh birth-certificate rule (Verification Charter v1.5 section 9) its mechanics: the certificate lives beside the mesh, hash-bound to it, and every workflow that lets a mesh enter a case asserts it at entry
rationale: The 2026-08-08 archive sweep (the mesh birth-certificate audit record of 2026-08-08) found 178 unique reachable meshes: 105 already certified, 47 clean-but-uncertified, and exactly one born broken -- the A3 vcoarse pyHyp mesh, which entered a case three times under reconstruction because nothing at entry asked for its certificate. The single biggest gap is structural, not individual: the mesh cache stores bare polyMesh with no quality record, so 400+ act-six, act-seven, act-nine and study run dirs carry a mesh with no record beside it even though geometry_study's gate DID run checkMesh at generation -- the reading was transient (L-40: the switch that ran must be provable from the artifact). Proposed mechanics, report-only, for Infra to adopt with their own verification: (1) certificate = log.checkMesh beside the case (existing convention) plus a hash-bound certificate sidecar beside every .mesh-cache entry carrying points_sha256, verdict, cells, maxAR, maxNonOrtho, maxSkew, generator, created_at. (2) Insertion points: the head engineer's mesh-cache save (~line 1006) writes the certificate at cache-save; cached_mesh_available (~971) treats a cache entry without a matching-hash certificate as NOT cached, which is the charter's quarantine; restore_cached_mesh (~986) asserts hash+verdict at entry and copies the certificate into the case. the DAFoam docker engine's mesh-cache mirror (~lines 216 to 250) gets identical mechanics -- this is the pyHyp entry path, the pathology's generator. the geometry workflow persists the log its gate judged (mesh_quality_reading ~455, retry_mesh_quality ~590, rung builder ~1388-1402) into the case dir and hands it to save_mesh_to_cache. the model-form batch script, already the exemplar (retained logs, hard gates at mesh_verdict ~569), adds assert-at-entry so an absent or unreadable log.checkMesh refuses the solver launch instead of surfacing as post-hoc exclusion. (3) Pre-registrations and docket items naming a mesh rung carry its points_sha256 plus verdict so a born-broken mesh cannot re-enter under a new case name.

cost_basis: measured; the audit's own 85 s of serial checkMesh is already spent, the mechanics themselves are code changes with no solver time
expected_knowledge_gain: Every mesh that enters an archive, a pre-registration, or a ladder rung is provably born clean at the artifact level, and a missing certificate is a refusal at entry rather than a forensic finding months later; the A3 vcoarse failure mode (same broken mesh, three case reconstructions, zero certificate checks) becomes unreachable
outcome: Adopted as Mesh Standard v1.1 section 6 after the supervisor re-verified the audit by hand: the born-broken A3 vcoarse specimen's checkMesh reproduces digit-for-digit (aspect ratio 2.08e95, 23 negative-volume cells), a born-clean certificate reproduces digit-for-digit, and the dedupe-by-points-hash claim holds. Implemented at all three mesh-cache layers plus a fourth chokepoint the proposal missed (the shock-bench module cache two unsteady workflows share): certificate at save from the case's own checkMesh record, quarantine at lookup for any entry without a matching-hash accepted certificate, certificate carried into the case at restore, the geometry workflow saving after its gate so the certificate is the gate's own persisted reading, and the model-form batch refusing a launch on an uncertified or breaching mesh with R12 exemptions preserved. A failed check never certifies. 22 tests; suite 1210 passed with zero failures.
